project.name: tower-connector-artifactory
project.description:
Confirms artifacts in JFrog Artifactory (ADR-021).
GET only, and that is not restraint — it is what the design bought. Artifactory's capable search is AQL, which is POST /api/search/aql, and ADR-001's structural form forbids a Connector from calling anything named post. Because the team tags an image and a chart with the version and the short commit, the coordinate is a function of what Tower already holds, so this asks a direct question at a direct address and never searches.
No JFrog client library. Tower reads whether a path exists, its checksum, its size and when the repository received it — four fields the JDK's own HTTP client reads in a few lines. A client library would pull a dependency tree to save nothing.
Not verifiable from where Tower is built. No JFrog host is reachable from this environment and Artifactory publishes no OpenAPI description for ADR-019's schema check, so this Connector stands where Jenkins and Jira stand: tested against a local server, with the live check outstanding in CHECKLIST.md. The API shapes it reads are written from knowledge rather than recorded off a real instance, which is a weaker footing than the GitHub Connector's and is recorded as such.
